rows.text: POET reads the poem aloud to the EX; the TV shows the world's chaos. the Severn, a high bedroom; the Hive's needles fill the window. dense orange fog at every hour; the sun is a disc or nothing. low-pressure sodium (the New Boroughs): a single orange wavelength that greys every other colour.
Haze at the window
rows.line: I look for a way out through the hallways, within the drawers and fire escapes, trip

rows.text: Off the fire escape
rows.line: on my own words, falling out of life, and find where you go when you leave.

rows.text: The fall montage — below the tower, into the black
rows.line: It was the maze constructed by a tainted love, a known yet unknown pit beneath the quicksands

rows.line: I failed at protecting you from your own vices, crashing the party of your evilest instincts

rows.line: And no tears and no fucks, no love to give, old to teach.

poems.title: How to Break off an Engagement

rows.text: The tambourine falls, flies, tumbles through black space and enters the chapel through a window, still whole. the chapel's seaward lancet. storm then calm; mist on the sea; dew burning off. the white ceramic itself, lit by the sky; mirror pools that hold the stars.
The empty temple — the nave, choir loft and baptistery as built
rows.line: pews taken by cobwebs, and doused in disintegration.

rows.text: Gifts at the side doors — the side doors and stone threshold
rows.line: Spirits have left salvations and opened gift boxes placed outside the side doors.

rows.text: The storm — the flat, from the beach
rows.line: It thunders, then it rains until nothing remains.

rows.text: Remnants on the shore — the tide line where the chapel stood

rows.text: POET stands on the shore at night, hands in pockets, no heart; walks looking at the decay and shattered pieces as ravens fly overhead. the shore below the rail, where the chapel's pieces washed east. wet stone, mist on the sea, a low sun. none of its own: dawn and dusk; a few lanterns on the steps; one sodium platform lamp left from the New Boroughs.
The silence — the shore looking out, then back to the trees
rows.line: The waves will calm to fold it whispers and the winds will mute the trees for the right level of silence

rows.text: The heart on the sand

Naming stars — the avenue through the field
rows.line: to ask if I can name my own stars, even galaxies if I may.

rows.text: Marble gates with wings swing open to an ancestral orchestra; a line of figures, the POET among them, walks through into the radiant city. the Light Gate, from the field. clear. the gate's white ceramic lit from inside; fences of light at the perimeter (cyan, high-frequency).
Road down, following comets
rows.line: welcome us. Poets who eased generations down yellow brick roads and plucked our souls out

rows.line: resurrecting Atlantis. Here we are all one. The pack we've made here with nature

rows.line: but here we are all safe. An unfamiliar flickering candlelight illuminating smiles

rows.line: at night where shadows cast from narrow streets beaming with love, and the joyful noises that

rows.text: Could stay forever, then wandering to the house
rows.line: it could stay here forever, leaving behind crosshairs for continuums and strains for

rows.text: Neon title over the booth; the DJ appears, spins, scratches; the fader slides and the crowd hushes waiting for the drop as the POET asks to be turned up. the House: the booth on the back wall. light rain, steam, teal haze. the Relighting: neon and string lights, candles in the alleys; teal and pink.
Eyes wide shut at the mic — the bar, facing the floor
rows.line: spoken words, I have a story to tell. Of ghosts whispering unfolded delusions, birthed in purity

rows.text: Ghosts in the speaker mesh — the speaker stacks
rows.line: treasures escaping and devaluing themselves after defamed unsalted stars diminish their glares.

rows.text: A thousand light years, into the red — between bar and booth
rows.line: And I've walked a thousand light years across the greatest divide to be heard. So DJ please turn me

rows.line: we love we not. Of a future gone swiftly and a past left empty handed to pick a road of heavy rain

rows.line: or a frontal fog or of dim night lights under a cloud with the silver lining. Of now turning

Mid-dance, a translucent soul rises out of the POET's chest and floats above; the emptied body keeps moving to the beat alone. the rooftop club on a spire crown (up the elevator shaft from the House). cloud below the platforms; clear above. violet and blue underlights on the stems; warm lamps on the platforms; the shaft's red.
Haze and the soul's return
rows.line: I want my soul now to imagine my body pulsing and head throbbing from the music and empty on

rows.text: Strangers collide; the last one to leave
rows.line: a crowded floor of sweated perfumes and temptations. Let's watch strangers collide and spark electric

rows.text: Soul over Atlantis, the open field at the equator
rows.line: bitter refraction inside the walls of an escape that few pleasures offer us. Now let us put my

rows.text: Angels' ice-water baptism — the middle of the club floor
rows.line: and much hotter. Cool me down by pouring unfiltered water out of the ice bath salted from the closest

Mountains from the rooftop — the parapet
rows.line: it is to finally get acquainted with the night, staring into unfamiliar yet relatable mountains

Friends arrive under a welcome-home banner; laughter and hugs with no reason; the circle forms. the hall under its rafters. storm then calm; mist on the sea; dew burning off. the white ceramic itself, lit by the sky; mirror pools that hold the stars.
Loud voices, overheard hearts — the centre of the gathering
rows.line: loud voices so our hearts can be overheard. My mind drifts into the darkness of our afterlives,

rows.text: The empty rooms of the afterlife
rows.line: and those rooms are empty. We are all here, each holding our glasses of burning sands

rows.text: Hourglasses and the group photo (archival reenactment)
rows.line: and known journeys, and grateful to every living tree in the forest for the shared years

rows.text: Trees at the forest edge
rows.line: and the shared memories. This is brotherhood. Smiles with no reason,

rows.text: Football in the meadow, then home
rows.line: brother's soul and follow paths of hilltops and canyons, of blinding lights and infinite nights,

rows.text: He sits at a corner table and observes couples at other tables, wanting to be noticed. the pier café's corner table. calm, bright; haze gathering off the water. daylight on water; at night the drowned gardens' own light (bioluminescent), fishermen's lamps in the cathedral.
Walk from the temple around the harbor
rows.line: with every pulsing beat after walking alone.

rows.line: I escaped here for a reason,
